The Problem: Manual Consolidation Is Breaking Under Pressure
, including regional branches, subsidiaries, and joint ventures, often across different countries, accounting standards, and systems.
Each entity may use its own ledger and ERP, which makes consolidation a highly manual, time-consuming process that’s also prone to errors.
Spreadsheets have become the default tool for stitching this data together. But
Teams must manually perform steps like currency conversions, intercompany eliminations, and account mapping. These activities consume days or even weeks as complexity increases.
Key pain points with manual spreadsheet workflows include:
Too many touchpoints: Finance teams download reports, map formats, reconcile issues, and revalidate data each period. Even small misalignments require deep investigation.
Inconsistent processes: Without standardized workflows, ledgers get consolidated differently depending on the controller or region. This leads to discrepancies and version control problems.
Late adjustments: Last-minute eliminations, foreign exchange recalculations, and journal entry reclassifications can derail close timelines.
Zero audit trail: Spreadsheets do not inherently track who made changes or why. This opacity increases audit risk and can trigger compliance flags.

Finance and accounting teams now spend up to one-third of their time on reconciliations alone. As a result, period-end becomes a reactive series of fixes and detective work rather than a strategic report delivery process.

In an industry with narrow margins and dynamic operations, relying on spreadsheets isn’t just inefficient. It introduces financial risk and stalls organizational agility. It becomes a major bottleneck that prevents finance teams from being true business partners.
